Chapter 171: 0168 Hero Chen Bids Farewell to the Literary World

Today was just a casual chat in Shanghai; a series of activities would follow when they went to Thousand Island Lake.

But even a casual chat needed a theme.

The theme at this moment was "The Literary World and the Market," namely, young writers had entered the market, but had they entered the literary world?

Na Duo was the first to speak, "I don't think we've entered the literary world yet. I've worked as an editor for 'Mengya,' published web novels, and also a series of novellas and short stories. But my readers are all young people, mostly students. I consider myself to be quite marketable, but how many people in the Writers' Association know my pen name? Teacher Yu Hua, do you know my pen name?"

Yu Hua said, "I know your real name, and I know your dad is the editor-in-chief of 'Mengya.'"

"But you don't know my pen name. Right?" Na Duo pressed.

Yu Hua let out a hearty laugh.

Na Duo said, "See? This proves that I've only entered the market, and not the literary world at all."

Cai Jun said, "I'm also one of those who dreamed of entering the literary world but couldn't find the way in, and eventually had to turn to the market. I have to say, the market is much easier to get into than the literary world."

Old Mr. Cheng Cun, who had been taking pictures all this time, lowered his digital camera and said, "Why are you so insistent on getting into the literary world? The literary world is an illusion to begin with. You can publish your own works, you have your own loyal readers, why bother with all that superficial nonsense?"

"We want to prove ourselves, to gain recognition from mainstream writers," Jiang Feng said.

Shi Ling said, "Xiao Fan and Jiang Feng, the two of them are in the most awkward position right now. They're both post-80s writers, but they write pure literary fiction. They lack both market appeal and a real entry into the literary world."

Ye Zhaoyan, Ye Shengtao's grandson, smiled and said, "Actually, it's more or less the same for everyone. Coming to this forum, I hear people calling me 'senior' everywhere. But who is whose senior? People like us, in our forties and fifties, we have to humor the next generation and comment on their works. And we also have to humor the previous generation, showing that we're still paying attention to the works of older writers. You want the seniors to see your works, and the seniors also want you to see theirs."

Zhang Yueran said, "Of course we're reading the seniors' works, but the seniors are definitely not reading ours."

"That's not necessarily true," Ge Fei said. "The older generation of writers will definitely pay attention to the next generation. Take Wei Hui, who is a bit older than you. She used 'body writing,' and Jia Pingwa secretly read her books."

Zhang Xinying smiled and said to Zhang Yueran, "Jia Pingwa has probably secretly read your works too, he just won't admit it for now. Writers like them definitely have to maintain an air of importance."

Ge Fei said, "Alright, let's not talk about this."

"Hahaha."

Everyone burst into laughter.

Chen Guiliang had been texting the whole time. It was too boring here, so he could only kill time by chatting with Bian Guanyue and Tao Xue.

Cao Wenxuan suddenly said, "I've carefully read Chen Guiliang's 'Those Things in the Ming Dynasty.' He has published three volumes, and I've read all three. I'm waiting for him to release the fourth."

Hearing his name, Chen Guiliang put down his phone and saw that everyone was looking at him. He said, "I just wrote it casually."

Cao Wenxuan asked, "Why haven't you joined the Beijing Writers' Association?"

"I filled out the application form, but it got lost when my company moved," Chen Guiliang said.

Cao Wenxuan said, "Then I'll have someone send another one over to you."

Hearing this, many of the young writers present cast envious glances at Chen Guiliang.

At this time, not just anyone could get into the Writers' Association.

Chen Guiliang just smiled and said nothing.

Su Tong said, "You should also express your opinion. About the literary world and the market."

Chen Guiliang said, "The literary world is just like the music scene or the film industry. It's nothing more than a circle that holds a certain authority due to various factors. I don't think there's any need to force one's way in. The writers in the literary world are all busy with 'underclass writing' right now. The young writers, on the other hand, are busy with 'market writing.' The two sides have no common ground."

"You even know about underclass writing?" Tie Yi smiled.

Chen Guiliang said, "It's the most mainstream thing in the literary world right now. Everyone should know about it, right?"

However, at least half of the young writers present paid no attention to underclass writing.

Some had not even heard of it.

Immediately, a couple of young writers quietly asked the friends next to them, "What's underclass writing?"

"No idea," their friends shook their heads.

Scar literature was long a thing of the past.

Youth literature had never become mainstream.

Underclass writing, which focused on disadvantaged groups, was the current literary mainstream.

It began brewing in 1994 and had a major explosion last year, with traditional writers flocking to it in droves.

This was true for Yu Hua, and also for Fang Fang.

The reason was the ever-widening gap between the rich and the poor, the increasingly severe social fragmentation, and the need for someone to speak up for the urban underclass and the peasants.

Some writers, the more they focused on the underclass, the more disappointed they became with reality, forming a mindset that would be fixed for the latter half of their lives.

They were trapped and couldn't get out, gradually developing a path dependency in their writing.

When the times completely changed, they still stuck to their old ways, resorting to fabrication when they couldn't find tragic prototypes, instead of seeking out the real new generation of disadvantaged groups.

This trend of thought permeated from the literary world into various other fields.

The underclass writing trend, which started with the intention of speaking for the people, quickly colluded with neoliberalism under the instigation of certain groups!

It became so muddled that it was hard to tell friend from foe, to distinguish who was human and who was a demon.

Some writers even became demons yet still felt good about themselves, thinking they were good people.

Ge Fei asked, "What's your take on underclass writing?"

"Speaking for the underclass is of course a good thing," Chen Guiliang said, "but when anything becomes mainstream, it's bound to evolve into a tool for some to gain fame and fortune. Especially underclass writing, this thing can bring a writer both. They can earn huge royalties on one hand, while pleading for the people on the other. To be honest, some of those works are disgusting to read."

"Why is underclass writing disgusting to read?" Wang Meng asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "The writers have been detached from the underclass for too long. They might have been part of the underclass once, but that was ten or twenty years ago. They take a tour of the urban-rural fringe, take a walk through a suburban village, and think they're familiar with the lives of the lower class. Some even just work behind closed doors, shooting an arrow first and then drawing the target, just making things up. It seems like they're speaking for the underclass, but the characters they write are just soulless props."

"This kind of literary work can only move the literary world and certain readers. The real people of the underclass feel no connection when they read it at all!"

Hearing this, the middle-aged and older writers all smiled.

Those smiles each held a different meaning.

Tie Yi quickly changed the subject, "I think the post-80s writers still need to accumulate more life experience. Your works as a whole seem immature, and the content is somewhat repetitive."

Since Chen Guiliang was no longer on his phone, he now decided to speak his mind freely. "I've also read Jiang Feng's novels. He's like a young Dugu Qiubai. His potential is astonishing, but he focuses too much on techniques. He'll be truly great when he becomes formless."

Chen Guiliang had actually read Jiang Feng's novels in his previous life.

Later on, in order to cater to the market, this person abandoned literary fiction and complex narrative techniques, and wrote a commercial novel that even he himself looked down upon.

However, that commercial novel turned out to be his magnum opus.

Jiang Feng was particularly surprised to hear Chen Guiliang's comment on him. "You don't think I should use those writing techniques?"

"You're showing off your skills. It's really not necessary," Chen Guiliang smiled. "Of course, this is just my personal opinion. Everyone has their own ideas. At least your class is much higher than mine. When 'Those Things in the Ming Dynasty' came out, many people said my writing style was like an elementary school student's."

Song Jingru asked, "Your writing in 'Journey Across the Vast Seas' is very good. Why did you make 'Those Things in the Ming Dynasty' so simple?"

"To make money," Chen Guiliang said. "Writing it more simply allows even elementary school students to understand it. Plus, it contains historical knowledge, which can entice parents to spend money and buy it for their kids."

"Hahaha!"

A wave of laughter filled the room.

Xiao Fan asked curiously, "Do you really have no literary pursuits?"

Chen Guiliang said, "I'm a very unrefined person. I really don't have any literary pursuits. I wrote 'Those Things in the Ming Dynasty' purely because I was afraid venture capital firms wouldn't come, and I wanted to use the royalties to keep the company afloat a while longer."

"I don't believe you. You were quite harsh when you criticized 'Wolf Totem' a few months ago," Xiao Fan said.

Chen Guiliang said, "It had nothing to do with literature. I just didn't like it, so I criticized it a little. Didn't you want to criticize it?"

Xiao Fan said, "I hadn't even read the book. I only went to a Xinhua Bookstore to check it out after seeing how fiercely you all were criticizing it."

"What did you think?" Chen Guiliang asked.

"I didn't even finish the first chapter. Reading that kind of book is a waste of time," Xiao Fan said.

Just then, Hu Weishi came over with two staff members, carrying a large stack of photocopied documents to distribute.

It was a list of works by all the writers present, along with excerpts of brilliant passages from their representative works.
